cohort: The study included 208 pregnant women who underwent a Caesarean Section at Queen Elizabeth Central Hospital (QECH) in Blantyre, Malawi, between February and July 2023.
finding: The overall cumulative incidence of Surgical Site Infections (SSIs) following Caesarean Section was 9.61%, with Staphylococcus aureus being the most common organism, and a high proportion of patients received antibiotics without specific bacterial isolation.
mod_finding: The study found a 9.61% incidence of SSIs following Caesarean Section and highlighted issues with antimicrobial use in this mode of birth, including resistance in some cases.
